title: MAKE THE BELIEF BET
goal: Let one behaviour test what argument cannot settle.

steps.action: State the belief as a clear prediction.
Choose a safe, small action that could prove it wrong as well as right.
Hold the expected result before acting.
Run the test, then compare observation with prediction.
Pay out only to evidence.

win: ✓ Evidence won the bet. Belief did not get a sympathy payout.
supports: Exhale after “Pay Out”; release the score.
I can use “Choose Safe” without perfecting.
formula_flow: State Belief → Choose Safe → Picture Outcome → Test Observation → Pay Out
safety:
PAUSE
Cancel any experiment involving danger, coercion, medical risk, or another person’s consent.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE EFFORT STAIRCASE
goal: Start where movement is possible, not where pride prefers.

steps.action: Name five versions of the task from almost easy to really stretching.
Remove the zero-effort decoy.
Do the smallest remaining version that leaves visible evidence—one paragraph, one call, one plate washed.
Next time, climb only one stair.

win: ✓ One stair was enough to create movement.
supports: Exhale after “Climb Stair”; release the score.
I can use “Cross Out” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Name → Cross Out → Remain Version → Climb Stair
safety:
PAUSE
Reduce the step further if illness, exhaustion, or overload is being ignored.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOOD HAS ALIBIS
goal: Test what the day does to the feeling.

steps.action: Choose one activity.
Before it, score expected mood; at the start, notice your actual mood; at the end, score again.
Add one sentence about what changed during the activity.
Repeat with three different actions before deciding ‘nothing helps.’

win: ✓ The feeling kept its voice but lost the judge’s chair.
supports: Exhale after “Try Three Ways”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Score Expected” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Choose Activity → Score Expected → Add Sentence → Try Three Ways
safety:
PAUSE
Seek professional support if low mood is severe, persistent, or linked to self-harm thoughts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TWO ENGINES
goal: Pleasure and mastery refuel different parts of you.

steps.action: For the next day, schedule one act chosen purely for enjoyment and one chosen for competence.
Make both small enough to happen.
After each activity, ask which engine it fed: pleasure or mastery. Rate that one channel only.
Do not demand that either activity fix everything.

win: ✓ Good-enough became usable again.
supports: Exhale after “Drop Demand”; release the score.
I can use “Make Small” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Schedule Chosen → Make Small → Check Both → Drop Demand
safety:
PAUSE
Rebalance if achievement becomes punishment or pleasure becomes avoidance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MAKE THE ROOM VOTE
goal: Your environment casts ballots before willpower arrives.

steps.action: Pick one desired behaviour and one unwanted default.
Place the first object needed for the desired action directly in your path.
Add one small obstacle to the unwanted route: distance, logout, container, timer, or removal.
Let the room make the better vote easier.

win: ✓ The room tipped the vote toward the choice I actually want.
supports: Exhale after “Let Space Vote”; release the score.
“Pick Desired” to “Let Space Vote”: what loosened?
I can use “Place Object” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Pick Desired → Place Object → Add Deliberate → Let Space Vote
safety:
PAUSE
Keep changes reversible and never block access to medication, food, safety, or essential contact.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE URGE MISS ITS APPOINTMENT
goal: The ritual expects you; do not show up.

steps.action: Name the cue and the usual calming act it normally summons.
Contact only a manageable dose of the cue.
Keep your hands and attention out of the ritual while the urge changes on its own.
Hold the peak and the first natural drop.
The learning comes from not doing the old ritual.

win: ✓ The urge stayed loud without taking the wheel.
supports: Exhale after “Let Learning Land”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Contact” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Name Cue → Contact → Keep Hands → Mark Peak → Let Learning Land
safety:
PAUSE
Use clinical guidance for severe OCD, addiction, eating disorders, or exposures that feel unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BODY VETO
goal: Install a movement the habit cannot do beside.

steps.action: Spot the first motor cue—reaching, picking, scrolling, biting, clenching.
Use a safe opposite posture and practise it slowly three times.
When the cue appears, enter that posture for ten seconds while naming the urge.
Then decide consciously.

win: ✓ Habit vetoed. The choice came back online.
supports: Exhale after “Decide Consciously”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Choose Safe” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Identify Motor → Choose Safe → Enter Posture → Decide Consciously
safety:
PAUSE
Choose another response if the posture causes pain, strain, or social risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHEN/THEN FIRMWARE
goal: Pre-decide the moment that usually steals the decision.

steps.action: Picture one line only: WHEN [specific visible cue], THEN I WILL [small physical action].
Remove vague words such as try, soon, or better.
Imagine the cue once, do the action once, and place the rule where the cue occurs.
Skip the pep talk.

win: ✓ Decision installed before motivation had a chance to bargain.
supports: Exhale after “Skip Pep Talk”; slow the clock.
“Picture Line” to “Skip Pep Talk”: what loosened?
I can use “Remove Vague” without rushing.
formula_flow: Picture Line → Remove Vague → Imagine Cue → Skip Pep Talk
safety:
PAUSE
Rewrite the rule if the trigger is unclear or the response depends on another person.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FIRST DRIFT
goal: Relapse announces itself quietly before it becomes a return.

steps.action: Trace the unwanted behaviour backward in your mind: first act, private permission, routine change, environment shift, body state.
Place a red dot on the earliest sign you could realistically notice.
Attach one simple interruption to that red dot and rehearse what you will do when it appears.

win: ✓ I found the drift point before the whole slide began.
supports: Gently exhale after “Plant Interrupt”; no forcing.
I can use “Mark Earliest” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Picture the Path → Mark Earliest → Tell Support
safety:
PAUSE
For substance withdrawal, overdose risk, or dangerous relapse, use medical and emergency support rather than self-management alone.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RIDE THE CRAVING GRAPH
goal: An urge is a curve pretending to be a command.

steps.action: Notice its current level and where it moves in the body.
Watch for slope: rising, flattening, cresting, falling.
Every thirty seconds, imagine the next point without acting on the urge.
When the line changes direction, name the change.
Choose what protects the next hour.

win: ✓ The craving curved; the next hour kept the vote.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Time”; let wanting crest.
I can use “Watch Slope” without obeying the urge.
formula_flow: Level → Watch Slope → Imagine Urge → Name Change → Choose Time
safety:
PAUSE
Cravings linked to withdrawal, overdose, or medical danger require professional help.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE VISIBLE VOTE
goal: Values become real only after the body votes.

steps.action: Choose a value and design its smallest public evidence: send the honest line, open the document, place the medicine beside water, step outside for two minutes.
Complete it before upgrading the plan.
A tiny enacted vote outranks a perfect private speech.

win: ✓ Made one tiny value-vote visible instead of keeping it private.
supports: Exhale after “Cast Tiny Vote”; release the score.
I can use “Complete Shift” without perfecting.
formula_flow: Choose Value → Complete Shift → Cast Tiny Vote
safety:
PAUSE
Scale down without shame if the action exceeds current capacity.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: OBJECTIVE OVER EGO
goal: The best move may not be the most satisfying proof.

steps.action: Picture the real objective in seven words or fewer.
Name the action that advances it and the action that merely wins, punishes, impresses, or avoids embarrassment.
Imagine tomorrow’s result after each.
Select what works, even if the ego receives no trophy.

win: ✓ The picture widened beyond the selected facts.
supports: Exhale after “Select Works”; slow the clock.
formula_flow: Picture Real → Name → Imagine Tomorrow → Select Works
safety:
PAUSE
Revisit the objective if it excludes dignity, consent, or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: COOL THE ALARM PANEL
goal: Temperature can reach body alarm before language does.

steps.action: Use cool—not painfully cold—water or a wrapped cool pack on the cheeks and around the eyes for a brief interval.
Slow your body while the sensation lands.
Remove it, name the room, and reassess the next safe action.
Treat the cool sensation as a reset cue. Stop before it becomes an endurance test.

win: ✓ The alarm cooled without turning discomfort into a test.
supports: Gently exhale after “End the Cool”; no breath-holding.
“End the Cool”: what changed from “Use Cool”?
I can use “Slow” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Use Cool → Slow → Remove Name → End the Cool
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid with medical contraindications; never use ice directly or hold your breath.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BURN THE EXCESS CHARGE
goal: Give body alarm a finish line.

steps.action: Choose a contained burst: fast stairs, wall pushes, brisk marching, or another safe vigorous movement.
Set a short timer before starting.
When it ends, stop completely, feel the after-pulse, and drink water.
Let the body spend energy without spending your future.

win: ✓ Panic became a wave with surroundings around it.
supports: Gently exhale after “Let Body”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Set Short” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Choose Burst → Set Short → End Completely → Let Body
safety:
PAUSE
Do not attempt intense movement with injury, illness, pregnancy concerns, or medical restrictions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE LONGER OUT-BREATH
goal: Make urgency leave through a gentler exit.

steps.action: Breathe in without pulling extra air.
Let the outflow last slightly longer, as though fogging a distant window silently.
Repeat only while comfortable; keep shoulders quiet and jaw loose.
After several rounds, resume natural breathing and look for one workable decision.

win: ✓ The craving lost its automatic route to action.
supports: Exhale after “Breathe Workable”; slow the clock.
I can use “Let Outflow” without rushing.
formula_flow: Breathe Pulling → Let Outflow → Repeat Comfortable → Breathe Workable
safety:
PAUSE
Return to ordinary breathing immediately if light-headed, air-hungry, or panicky.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STAY FOR THE UPDATE
goal: Safe contact gives fear new data.

steps.action: Choose an external cue low enough on your fear ladder to approach voluntarily.
Enter without escape and remain until you observe at least one mismatch between prediction and reality.
Name the mismatch before leaving.
Repeat later under safe conditions rather than chasing maximum distress.

win: ✓ The future reopened beyond the alarm.
supports: Exhale after “Repeat Later”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Enter Escape” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Choose External → Enter Escape → Name Mismatch → Repeat Later
safety:
PAUSE
Exposure needs clinical support when trauma, medical risk, severe phobia, or feeling unreal or disconnected is involved.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE CONTROLLED REPLAY
goal: A feared scene needs a container, not a flood.

steps.action: Set a start time, endpoint, grounding object, and recovery plan.
Recount or visualise the feared scene at a manageable pace without changing key facts.
Notice shifts in prediction or emotion across the telling.
Finish by naming present location and date.

win: ✓ Replay closed in the present: current place, current date, current choice.
supports: Exhale after “Finish Location”; notice the room.
I can use “Recount” to return here.
formula_flow: Set Time → Recount → Prediction → Finish Location
safety:
PAUSE
Do not self-administer for severe trauma, psychosis, acute crisis, or destabilising memories.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LEAVE ONE QUESTION OPEN
goal: Uncertainty can remain unfinished without becoming an emergency.

steps.action: Choose a low-stakes unknown.
Picture it on a card and forbid checking, asking, or mentally solving until a set time.
Carry the unanswered card while doing normal life.
At review, notice what the urge did—not whether certainty arrived.

win: ✓ The unanswered part stopped demanding immediate closure.
supports: Exhale after “Watch The Urge”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Picture Card” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Choose Low → Picture Card → Carry Unanswered → Watch The Urge
safety:
PAUSE
Begin with smaller unknowns if abstaining causes overwhelming distress.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STAY THROUGH RECOVERY
goal: Stay long enough to learn what happens after the peak.

steps.action: During a safe practice round, notice the highest point and the first downward shift.
Do not leave at that first relief.
Remain with the cue through a visible recovery phase—steady gaze, slower movement, reduced urge—then end on purpose.
Departure follows learning, not panic.

win: ✓ Exit came after recovery—not at panic’s command.
supports: Gently exhale after “Leave After Recovery”; no breath-holding.
I can use “Stay Past Relief” while alarm rises.
formula_flow: Highest → Stay Past Relief → Remain Cue → Leave After Recovery
safety:
PAUSE
Leave immediately if circumstances become genuinely unsafe or sense of where you are deteriorates.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMOVE ONE INVISIBLE CRUTCH
goal: A crutch can hide the safety already holding you.

steps.action: During a manageable practice round, spot one protective act that is unnecessary: gripping, rehearsing, sitting by the exit, checking pulse, carrying extra certainty.
Drop only that act while keeping legitimate safety intact.
Observe what the outcome says without it.

win: ✓ Pressure separated from importance.
supports: Exhale after “Observe Outcome”; slow the clock.
I can use “Drop Legitimate” without rushing.
formula_flow: Identify Protective → Drop Legitimate → Observe Outcome
safety:
PAUSE
Never remove medically required or genuinely protective behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE THE LESSON
goal: Learning that works in one room may not travel by itself.

steps.action: Repeat a mastered practice while changing one feature: location, time, cue order, duration, or intensity.
On the next round, alter a different feature.
Keep a small mental map of where the skill still works.
Let variation turn a local success into portable knowledge.

win: ✓ The lesson travelled. It no longer belongs to one room.
supports: Exhale after “Make Portable”; keep both sides.
I can use “Change Again” before concluding.
formula_flow: Repeat Mastered → Round → Keep Small → Turn Local
safety:
PAUSE
Vary only within the established safe range.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE TWO-CUE MERGE
goal: Combine mastered signals only after each can stand alone.

steps.action: Select two triggers already manageable separately.
Predict what joining them will add.
Contact both at a modest dose while dropping unnecessary escape.
Stay long enough to compare the combined result with the prediction, then recover fully.

win: ✓ Fear kept a warning, not a prophecy.
supports: Exhale after “Stay Long”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Predict Joining” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: Select Triggers → Predict Joining → Drop Unnecessary → Stay Long
safety:
PAUSE
Do not compound unmastered trauma cues or exceed the planned tolerance range.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TAKE SAFETY ON TOUR
goal: A lesson becomes reliable when the address changes.

steps.action: Pick a different secure setting for a skill already learned elsewhere.
Before entering, recall the earlier evidence in one sentence.
Practise, notice what transfers, and spot any context-specific obstacle.
Leave with a local reminder for next time.

win: ✓ The evidence field stopped being edited by one conclusion.
supports: Exhale after “Leave Local”; keep both sides.
I can use “Enter Earlier” before concluding.
formula_flow: Choose Safe → Enter Earlier → Practise Transfers → Leave Local
safety:
PAUSE
Use supported settings when unfamiliar places create major risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TURN UP THE WHISPER
goal: A tiny movement may be the body’s unfinished instruction.

steps.action: Notice the smallest spontaneous tendency: sway, curl, stretch, turn, reach.
Enlarge it by only ten percent and pause.
Check if it brings ease, protection, energy, or nothing.
Let the answer determine whether to continue, reverse, or stop.

win: ✓ The whisper became clear enough to guide the next choice.
supports: Gently exhale after “Let Determine”; no forcing.
I can use “Pause Enlarge” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Smallest → Pause Enlarge → Ask Whether → Let Determine
safety:
PAUSE
Keep amplitude small around pain, injury, or unstable balance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DATE-STAMP THE PRESENT
goal: Give the body proof that time has moved.

steps.action: Say the full date, your current age, location, and who is here.
Name three differences between now and the remembered danger: exits, resources, authority, distance, or choice.
Touch one present object while stating, ‘This object belongs to the present.’

win: ✓ The mind returned from elsewhere without needing a perfect landing.
supports: Gently exhale after “State Belongs”; orient to now.
I can use “Name Differences” while staying in now.
formula_flow: Say Age → Name Differences → State Belongs
safety:
PAUSE
Use immediate professional help if you cannot regain sense of where you are or safety.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: FEAR WITHOUT THE MOVIE
goal: At the peak, meet energy before narrative claims it.

steps.action: If safely steady, locate the most intense fear sensation and say only its movement, charge, heat, and boundary.
Remove prediction briefly.
Keep one hand or gaze anchored in the room.
Let raw body alarm be observed without following its film script.

win: ✓ Fear became body energy before it could become a movie.
supports: Exhale after “Let Raw”; then keep moving.
I can use “Remove Prediction” before motivation.
formula_flow: Locate Most → Remove Prediction → Keep Hand → Let Raw
safety:
PAUSE
Do not attempt at overwhelming intensity, active danger, or trauma flooding.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: STUDY THE REACTION, NOT THE CHARACTER
goal: Self-inquiry works better as disciplined research.

steps.action: Choose a reaction that happens often and remember three times it happened.
For each time, notice the trigger, meaning, body feeling, action, and result.
Compare the three examples with a trusted idea or guide.
Choose one idea to test. Leave your whole character out of the experiment.

win: ✓ One reaction became a testable clue, not a character verdict.
supports: Gently exhale after “Test One Guess”; no forcing.
I can use “Read Pattern” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Choose Recurring → Read Pattern → Compare Trusted → Test One Guess
safety:
PAUSE
Pause study when reflection becomes self-surveillance or shame.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: WHAT REMAINS WHEN REWARD LEAVES?
goal: Duty becomes clearer after fear and praise exit the room.

steps.action: Name your role, the people affected, and the values governing it.
Mentally remove applause, punishment, and personal advantage.
Ask which responsibility still stands.
Convert that answer into a time-bound action and one limit on what the role does not require.

win: ✓ The reward disappeared; the part I still cared about stayed.
supports: Exhale after “Set Role Limit”; keep the compass.
I can use “Remove Applause” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Name Role → Remove Applause → Ask Responsibility → Set Role Limit
safety:
PAUSE
Reject duties that violate safety, ethics, consent, or lawful limits.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: DEDICATE THE MOVE
goal: A larger recipient can change the flavour of effort.

steps.action: Select a behaviour; spot who or what it serves beyond immediate reward: a child, patient, craft, community, future generation, or principle.
do the act as an offering to that recipient.
Keep quality high even if nobody knows.

win: ✓ The effort felt different once it belonged to something larger than me.
supports: Gently exhale after “Keep Quality”; no forcing.
I can use “Act Offering” while sensation stays.
formula_flow: Select Behaviour → Act Offering → Keep Quality
safety:
PAUSE
Do not dedicate self-harm, overwork, or boundary violations as virtue.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE FIVE-BRICK REPAIR
goal: Reconnection is built from specific materials.

steps.action: Build five bricks in order: the event without spin; the impact without defence; your responsibility without dilution; the unmet need; one concrete repair action.
Decide what changed behaviour would look like over time.
Treat the apology as the doorway and the changed behaviour as the proof.

win: ✓ I rebuilt repair from five bricks, not from one polished apology.
supports: Exhale after “Make It Real”; release extra blame.
“Make It Real”: what changed from “Build Repair”?
I can use “Ask Evidence” without owning everything.
formula_flow: Build Repair → Ask Evidence → Apology
safety:
PAUSE
Do not seek reconnection where safety, consent, or accountability is absent.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE THE CHARGE INTO A CONTAINER
goal: Body alarm needs a route with walls.

steps.action: Choose shaking, pushing a wall, stamping, stretching, or strong walking.
Define space, duration, and maximum intensity before starting.
Keep movement nonviolent and stop at the timer.
Stand still afterward until you notice the earliest settling marker.

win: ✓ Gave the charge a container and stayed long enough to feel it settle.
supports: Exhale after “Take Earliest Move”; then keep moving.
“Choose Shaking” versus “Take Earliest Move”: what eased?
I can use “Start Define” before motivation.
formula_flow: Choose Shaking → Start Define → Keep Movement → Take Earliest Move
safety:
PAUSE
Stop for pain, dizziness, aggression, or loss of action control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ANGER WITH WALLS
goal: Power may be expressed without becoming a weapon.

steps.action: Choose a private space and a short timer.
State the anger plainly. Then imagine pushing the charge into a wall, or press your palms together firmly for a few seconds—without rehearsing violence.
When time ends, open hands, name the boundary underneath, and select a safe action.

win: ✓ Anger kept its power and lost its weapon.
supports: Exhale after “Open Hands”; release extra load.
I can use “State Anger” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Choose Private → State Anger → Open Hands
safety:
PAUSE
Leave immediately and get help if there is risk of harming anyone or damaging property.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BREAK THE DEADLINE MONOLITH
goal: Time pressure shrinks when it gains windows.

steps.action: Count the usable work blocks remaining, subtracting sleep and fixed duties.
Give each block one deliverable with a visible finish.
Place buffers before the final deadline.
Start the earliest window; refuse to mentally carry later windows inside it.

win: ✓ The decision regained enough space to be a decision.
supports: Exhale after “Start Earliest”; slow the clock.
I can use “Give Block” without rushing.
formula_flow: Count Usable → Give Block → Place Buffers → Start Earliest
safety:
PAUSE
Renegotiate scope early when the arithmetic is impossible.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: TWENTY SECONDS BEFORE THE STORY
goal: Let sensation stay fluid before language freezes it.

steps.action: For twenty seconds, ban emotion names and causes.
Say only geometry and physics: shape, temperature, pressure, texture, direction, pulse.
At the bell, choose the smallest Name that fits, or keep it unnamed if none does.

win: ✓ Sensation stayed fluid long enough to avoid becoming a premature story.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Smallest”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Describe Geometry” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: Name Causes → Describe Geometry → Choose Smallest
safety:
PAUSE
Stop internal focus if it triggers panic, feeling unreal or disconnected, or pain concern.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NO-CONCEPT MINUTE
goal: Reality gets one minute without explanation.

steps.action: Set a brief interval.
During it, do not create causes, labels, comparisons, or solutions.
Attend to direct colour, sound, contact, and movement.
If a concept appears, acknowledge ‘explanation’ and let the sensory world continue.

win: ✓ For one minute, reality did not need my commentary.
supports: Exhale after “Let Sensory”; notice the room.
I can use “Name Comparisons” to return here.
formula_flow: Set Brief → Name Comparisons → Attend Direct → Let Sensory
safety:
PAUSE
Concept fasting must not delay necessary decisions or medical care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MUTE THE INNER SUBTITLES
goal: One ordinary event requires no running review.

steps.action: Choose washing, walking, eating, or dressing.
For the duration, omit internal narration and meet only sensation and movement.
When commentary resumes, do not answer it; rejoin the activity at the next contact point.

win: ✓ The subtitles quieted enough for the activity to come back.
supports: Exhale after “Rejoin Activity”; notice the room.
I can use “Duration” to return here.
formula_flow: Choose Washing → Duration → Rejoin Activity
safety:
PAUSE
Keep internal language available for safety-critical tasks.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: RUN THE TWO-WORD TASK
goal: Focus needs one live command, not the whole project shouting at once.

steps.action: Look at the task and choose the single action verb needed for the next minute: read, compare, type, sort, call, or check.
Choose the exact object receiving that action: paragraph, invoice, shelf, patient Name, pan, or message.
Join them into a two-word command such as TYPE SUMMARY or SORT RECEIPTS. Hide every other instruction for now.
Run the command for sixty to ninety seconds. Stop only when the verb or object really needs to change.

win: ✓ The task stayed tiny enough to keep moving.
supports: One exhale after “Run Command”; redirect attention.
I can use “Pick Verb” amid noise.
formula_flow: Scan Work → Pick Verb → Bind Object → Run Command
safety:
PAUSE
Keep full protocols visible for clinical, legal, financial, driving, medication, machinery, or other safety-critical work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE RELEVANCE BOUNCER
goal: Information must show a present purpose at the door.

steps.action: Before opening, reading, or following an input, ask whether it changes a current decision, action, or safety need.
If no, route it to later, reference, or delete.
If yes, name the exact use before granting attention.

win: ✓ Information had to show its ID before attention let it in.
supports: One exhale after “Grant Attention”; redirect attention.
I can use “Route It” amid noise.
formula_flow: Open Input → Route It → Grant Attention
safety:
PAUSE
Permit restorative curiosity and leisure without forcing productivity tests.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CLOSE THE ATTENTION TABS
goal: Interrupted tasks leave residue until a restart point exists.

steps.action: Visit each abandoned item briefly.
Hold the immediate resumption move and choose close, schedule, delegate, or resume.
Do not do the tasks during the sweep.
End with one protected active tab and a written return address for the rest.

win: ✓ One tab stayed active; the others finally got a return address.
supports: One exhale after “End Active”; redirect attention.
I can use “Name Immediate Need” amid noise.
formula_flow: Visit → Name Immediate Need → Don't Perform → End Active
safety:
PAUSE
Limit the sweep if inventory becomes another avoidance project.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE EMOTION STOPS AT THE SKIN
goal: Another person’s state is information, not automatic duty.

steps.action: Notice where their emotion seems to enter your body.
Trace your physical boundary with gaze or touch.
State what action is yours, what remains theirs, and what you can offer without taking ownership.
Adjust distance if the distinction stays blurred.

win: ✓ Their emotion stopped at their skin; my duty stopped there too.
supports: Exhale after “Stay Blurred”; release extra load.
I can use “Trace Physical” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Emotion → Trace Physical → State Action → Stay Blurred
safety:
PAUSE
Honour mandated or genuine care responsibilities rather than withdrawing reflexively.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: OPEN THE IDENTITY PORTFOLIO
goal: One role should not own every share of self.

steps.action: Name five identities active in your life and estimate how much attention each received this week.
Choose the neglected role that still matters.
do one tiny action from its perspective today—friend, learner, neighbour, artist, caregiver, citizen.

win: ✓ I opened another share of myself and acted from it today.
supports: Exhale after “Use Another Share”; mark the pause.
I can use “Choose Neglected” before autopilot.
formula_flow: Estimate Much → Choose Neglected → Use Another Share
safety:
PAUSE
Do not use role expansion to avoid urgent responsibilities in the dominant role.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: REMOVE THE AUDIENCE
goal: Find the choice that survives without witnesses.

steps.action: Imagine nobody will see, praise, criticise, repost, or hear about the action.
Erase the imagined audience one row at a time.
What would you choose if only direct consequences and values remained?
Take the smallest version privately.

win: ✓ Loss did not erase every direction.
supports: Exhale after “Take Smallest”; keep the compass.
I can use “Erase Audience” while pain stays real.
formula_flow: Imagine Nobody → Erase Audience → Choose Direct → Take Smallest
safety:
PAUSE
Keep consultation where decisions emotion other people.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: MOVE THE MEMORY CAMERA
goal: You can preserve facts without re-entering the old viewpoint.

steps.action: Place the memory on a screen with enough visual distance.
View the scene from above, behind, or beside a compassionate observer.
Keep events accurate while changing camera position.
Add current-you outside the frame with present resources.

win: ✓ The memory camera moved, and the present kept its own frame.
supports: Exhale after “Add Resources”; drop the scoreboard.
I can use “View Scene” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Place Memory → View Scene → Keep Events → Add Resources
safety:
PAUSE
Traumatic memory perspective work should be supported if destabilising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ASK WHAT THE MEMORY IS STILL BILLING
goal: The memory can submit one claim without replaying the entire case.

steps.action: State the event as one factual headline with no motive and no sensory replay.
Finish this sentence once: ‘This memory still seems to demand ___.’ Keep only one claim.
Route the claim to BOUNDARY, REPAIR, GRIEF, or IMPOSSIBLE REVERSAL. Do not create a fifth category.
Choose the matching present response: set protection, request safe repair, make room for grief, or stop billing today for a reversal history cannot provide.

win: ✓ The old bill met today’s receipt—and stopped charging the present.
supports: Exhale after “Act Present”; end the lap.
I can use “Extract Claim” without another lap.
formula_flow: Headline Event → Extract Claim → Route Bill → Act Present
safety:
PAUSE
Do not contact unsafe people, seek revenge, force reconciliation, or use this game during trauma flooding or immediate danger.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE LAPSE FIRE DRILL
goal: One miss should trigger recovery, not identity collapse.

steps.action: Pre-plan three actions after a lapse: name what happened without judgement; restore the environment or schedule; do the next smallest valid repetition.
Store the script beside the behaviour.
Use it after one miss—before a second is negotiated.

win: ✓ The comparison sting stayed local instead of becoming a life verdict.
supports: Exhale after “Use After”; drop the scoreboard.
Keep one lesson: “Name What Happened” → “Use After”.
I can use “Store” without ranking my worth.
formula_flow: Name What Happened → Store → Use After
safety:
PAUSE
Escalate to support when lapses involve danger, relapse, or repeated loss of control.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: UNDERSTAND, THEN DISAGREE CLEANLY
goal: Empathy does not sign their conclusion.

steps.action: Summarise their view until they could recognise it.
Name the need or logic you understand.
Then say exactly where your meaning, value, or decision differs.
No ‘but’ inside the summary; disagreement receives its own sentence.

win: ✓ I understood their view without signing their conclusion.
supports: Exhale after “Receive Own”; let feeling settle.
I can use “Name Need” while emotion stays loud.
formula_flow: View They → Name Need → Say Meaning → Receive Own
safety:
PAUSE
Do not require mutual understanding before protecting yourself.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: ONE FIGHT, THREE TIME SCALES
goal: Today’s argument should not impersonate the whole relationship.

steps.action: Check the immediate issue, the recurring pattern, and the full relationship history separately.
Give each its own conclusion and action. Say what happened as if you were reporting it.
Do not let a good history erase a harmful pattern or one incident erase all context.

win: ✓ One fight found its proper scale—without erasing the history or excusing the pattern.
supports: Exhale after “Don't Erase”; soften the jaw.
I can use “Give Own” without extra heat.
formula_flow: Issue Recurring → Give Own → Don't Erase
safety:
PAUSE
Prioritise present safety regardless of historical positives.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: BURY THE GOAL, FREE THE ENERGY
goal: Some ambitions deserve a formal ending.

steps.action: Name the goal, why it once mattered, what changed, and which obligations can now close.
Thank any value it revealed.
Cancel one concrete commitment, archive materials, and redirect the recovered resource toward a living priority.

win: ✓ I buried the dead goal and redirected the energy to something alive.
supports: Exhale after “Bury the Goal”; watch the thought.
“Name Goal” versus “Bury the Goal”: what eased?
I can use “Keep Value” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Name Goal → Keep Value → Bury the Goal
safety:
PAUSE
Distinguish wise closure from quitting during a temporary setback.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THE UNANSWERED URGE EXPERIMENT
goal: Extra certainty can wait while its appetite changes.

steps.action: When the question demands an answer, picture it and delay asking for a short, chosen interval.
Track urge intensity at beginning, middle, and end without researching.
Decide afterward whether information is still needed for action or only for relief.

win: ✓ The urge for certainty changed before another answer was purchased.
supports: Exhale after “Decide Afterward”; leave it unanswered.
I can use “Track Urge” without a guarantee.
formula_flow: Question Demands → Track Urge → Decide Afterward
safety:
PAUSE
Do not delay answers required for health, safety, or deadlines.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: POSSIBLE IS NOT PROBABLE
goal: Separate existence from likelihood and support.

steps.action: State three lines: It is possible that…; It is probable that…; The evidence currently supports….
Do not allow content to migrate upward without justification.
Base planning on chance and safety margin, not possibility alone.

win: ✓ Possible and probable finally stopped sharing a name tag.
supports: Exhale after “Plan Probability”; leave the forecast.
I can use “Don't Allow” while fear stays loud.
formula_flow: State Lines → Don't Allow → Plan Probability
safety:
PAUSE
Low-probability high-impact risks may still justify proportionate precautions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THIS IS A CHAPTER, NOT THE BOOK
goal: The present cannot predict unopened pages.

steps.action: Position today’s event on a long timeline with past chapters already survived and blank space ahead.
Picture three future signposts that remain possible but unknown.
Choose one sentence describing this chapter accurately without making it the title of the whole life.

win: ✓ Today became a chapter again, not the title of the book.
supports: Exhale after “Choose Sentence”; loosen the label.
I can use “Picture Future” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Place Today → Picture Future → Choose Sentence
safety:
PAUSE
Avoid future projection when immediate crisis requires present support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: THOUGHTS MUST BRING AN AGENDA
goal: Extended thinking is earned by a clear question and output.

steps.action: Before giving a topic more time, require two items: the exact question and the form of a useful result—decision, plan, explanation, message, or acceptance.
If either is missing, deny the session and return to direct life.

win: ✓ The thought failed the agenda test, so it did not get a meeting.
supports: Exhale after “Return Direct”; loosen the label.
I can use “Return Direct” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Give Topic → Return Direct
safety:
PAUSE
Allow free reflection and creativity when productivity is not the purpose.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CALL THE MENTAL MEETING TO ORDER
goal: Concerns interrupt because none has an allocated agenda.

steps.action: Picture each topic as a meeting item with desired decision, time allowance, and required evidence.
Order by consequence and deadline.
Process only the first item; place every interruption in the parking lot for its scheduled turn.

win: ✓ One concern got the floor; the rest went to their scheduled seats.
supports: Exhale after “Place Interruption”; loosen the label.
I can use “Order” without becoming the label.
formula_flow: Picture Topic → Order → Place Interruption
safety:
PAUSE
Keep capacity for emergencies that legitimately override the agenda.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: NOTICE THE SPACE DOING THE HOLDING
goal: Objects dominate because intervals are treated as nothing.

steps.action: Choose three forms.
Attend to the space inside openings, around edges, and between objects.
Reverse figure and ground until space becomes as perceptible as matter.
Include the room around your body.

win: ✓ Noticed the empty space doing part of the holding.
supports: Exhale after “Include Room”; watch the thought.
I can use “Attend Space” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Choose Forms → Attend Space → Reverse Figure → Include Room
safety:
PAUSE
Maintain object focus where navigation or task precision demands it.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: LET THE WATCHER GO TOO
goal: Witnessing can become another identity to defend.

steps.action: Notice the subtle position that says ‘I am the observer.’ Treat that position, effort, or location as another known experience.
Allow awareness without maintaining a separate watcher.
Ground through ordinary action immediately afterward.

win: ✓ Even the watcher stepped down; ordinary life took the seat back.
supports: Exhale after “Release the Watcher”; watch the thought.
I can use “Allow Awareness” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Subtle → Allow Awareness → Release the Watcher
safety:
PAUSE
Do not attempt when self-experience is unstable or unreal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE SYMBOL’S JOB
goal: Unspoken experience may respond to transformation before explanation.

steps.action: Choose the image or object that represents the state.
Alter one property—open the cage, cool the metal, add roots, repair the crack, move the weight, give the storm a shoreline.
Observe the inner response and translate it into one practical move.

win: ✓ The mind produced content; it did not produce a commander.
supports: Exhale after “Observe Inner”; watch the thought.
I can use “Open Cage” without obeying thought.
formula_flow: Choose Image → Open Cage → Observe Inner
safety:
PAUSE
End the exercise when imagery grows disturbing, bizarre, or detached from reality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CONSTRAINTS ENTER BEFORE OPTIONS
goal: Must-have limits should shape the field before desire fills it.

steps.action: Picture safety, ethics, consent, resources, and timing constraints first.
Eliminate choices that violate them.
Generate options only inside the surviving space.
Treat creativity as solving within reality, not arguing with the boundary.

win: ✓ I let the constraints shape the field before the options started campaigning.
supports: Exhale after “Lead With Constraints”; release extra load.
I can use “Eliminate” without carrying it all.
formula_flow: Picture Safety → Eliminate → Generate → Lead With Constraints
safety:
PAUSE
Challenge assumed constraints that lack factual support.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
